newly_closed: the degree-below-k representatives and the regular principal tail are complementary submodules
the ambient polynomial module modulo the regular principal tail is linearly equivalent to degree-below-k polynomials
the regular quotient is linearly equivalent to k coefficient vectors and therefore has an explicit finite free basis
the image of every ideal containing the regular polynomial is exactly its bounded coefficient module under the quotient equivalence
the ideal-image and bounded-part coefficient modules are linearly equivalent
limitations: This closes the finite free quotient and containing-ideal image associated with the first supplied regular polynomial. The historical quotient of the paired G_1/M_1 modules, iteration through later-variable ground ideals, Smith coefficients, determinant norms, primitive resultants, compatible zeros, and multiplicities remain open.
